title: Keema Pie
subtitle: A spiced lamb mince pie in a British shortcrust case
excerpt: Lamb mince cooked with tomatoes, peas and warming spices, then baked inside a shortcrust case. A British curry-house twist on the classic mince pie.
sourceNotes: British curry-house pie tradition using keema as the filling, adapted for a standard 23cm pie dish.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the baked pie in slices, or freeze the filling separately. Reheat from frozen at 180C.
recipe.batchNotes: The keema filling doubles well. Freeze the extra in portions for future pies.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the keema filling up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate. Assemble on the day.

content.text: Keema is spiced minced lamb cooked with tomatoes and peas. It makes a natural pie filling because it is already thick and well seasoned. Cook it down until nearly dry before assembling. A wet keema will soak the base and make it hard to slice.

items.prepNote: two thirds for the base, one third for the lid

content.text: Heat the oil in the frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the onion and cook for 10 minutes until deep golden. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the cumin, coriander, turmeric and chilli powder. Stir for 1 minute in the oil until fragrant.
Add the lamb mince. Cook, breaking it apart, until browned all over. Drain off excess fat if needed.

Add the tinned tomatoes. Stir well and simmer uncovered for 20 to 25 minutes until the mixture is thick and most of the liquid has gone. Stir in the frozen peas and garam masala. Season with salt. Leave to cool completely.
Heat the oven to 200C. Roll out two thirds of the pastry and line the pie dish, leaving a little overhang.
Spoon the cold filling into the case. Roll the remaining pastry for a lid. Brush the rim with beaten egg, press the lid on and crimp firmly. Cut two slits in the top.
Brush all over with beaten egg. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the pastry is deep golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The filling is wet and leaks from the sides.
items.cause: The keema was not reduced for long enough before assembling.
items.fix: The filling should look nearly dry in the pan before it goes into the pie. Keep simmering with the lid off.

items.symptom: The pastry base is raw at the centre.
items.cause: The pie was on a cold shelf or the filling was still warm.
items.fix: Cool the filling fully. Bake the pie on a preheated baking sheet on a low oven shelf.

items.cause: The spices were not bloomed in the oil before the meat was added.
items.fix: Always stir the spices into the onion and oil for a full minute before adding anything wet. This releases the flavour.
